name: openverse
description: Openverse (openverse.org) is a search engine for openly licensed images and audio. This CLI calls its public REST API at api.openverse.org/v1 to search media, get item details and related items, fetch audio waveforms and oEmbed data, list content sources, and check the anonymous rate limit.

commands.name: search-images
commands.summary: Search openly licensed images by keyword, with filters for license, category, aspect ratio, size, source, tags and creator

params.name: q
params.description: Search keywords

params.name: page
params.description: Result page number, starting at 1

params.name: page_size
params.description: Results per page. Anonymous requests are capped at 20.

params.name: license
params.description: Comma-separated license codes, e.g. by,by-sa,by-nd,by-nc,by-nc-sa,by-nc-nd,cc0,pdm

params.name: license_type
params.description: Comma-separated usage permissions the license must allow

params.name: category
params.description: Image category

params.name: aspect_ratio
params.description: Image aspect ratio

params.name: size
params.description: Image size

params.name: source
params.description: Comma-separated source names, e.g. flickr,wikimedia (see list-image-sources)

params.name: tags
params.description: Match images with these tags

params.name: creator
params.description: Match images by this creator name

commands.name: get-image-oembed
commands.summary: Get oEmbed data for an Openverse image page URL, for embedding with attribution

params.name: url
params.description: Openverse image page URL in the form https://openverse.org/image/<id>, where <id> is the image UUID from search-images

commands.name: list-image-sources
commands.summary: List all image content sources (e.g. flickr, wikimedia) with their media counts

commands.name: search-audio
commands.summary: Search openly licensed audio by keyword, with filters for category, length, file extension, license and source

params.name: q
params.description: Search keywords

params.name: page
params.description: Result page number, starting at 1

params.name: page_size
params.description: Results per page. Anonymous requests are capped at 20.

params.name: category
params.description: Audio category

params.name: length
params.description: Audio duration bucket

params.name: extension
params.description: File extension, e.g. mp3, ogg, flac, wav

params.name: license
params.description: Comma-separated license codes, e.g. by,by-sa,cc0,pdm

params.name: license_type
params.description: Comma-separated usage permissions the license must allow

params.name: source
params.description: Comma-separated source names, e.g. freesound,jamendo (see list-audio-sources)

commands.name: list-audio-sources
commands.summary: List all audio content sources (e.g. freesound, jamendo) with their media counts

commands.name: get-rate-limit
commands.summary: Show the current API rate-limit status for this client (requests used and remaining)

notes: All commands call the public API at api.openverse.org/v1, not the openverse.org frontend. The frontend sits behind a Cloudflare bot check, and robots.txt disallows /search/. The only recorded request was a 307 on the openverse.org homepage (E1). These commands are built from the explorer's description of the documented API at api.openverse.org/v1/.

The example IDs for get-image, get-related-images, get-image-oembed, get-audio, get-related-audio and get-audio-waveform are placeholders, because no real UUID was captured. Run search-images or search-audio first and pass a result's id field. These examples will fail verification until real IDs are substituted.
The search-images and search-audio examples ('cat', 'piano') are common keywords, not queries copied from the recording.
Anonymous limits are 20 requests per minute and 200 per day. Use get-rate-limit to check the remaining quota, and keep page_size at 20 or below.

Combining a narrow filter with page 2 can return an empty results array. In the recording this happened with filtered image and audio queries, and also on page 2 of a plain image search. Check the result_count and page_count fields in the raw response before paging further.
Sort order was not tested, so no sort parameter is exposed. No search-suggestion (as-you-type) endpoint was found. All commands are read-only, and none need login.
